raw_response:
I'm 71 this year, and I've been farming these same fields for 50 years. It's just me and my husband at home now—our children work in Shijiazhuang and only come back for Spring Festival. We have 12 mu of land, but two old people can't work like we used to, so I have to be careful with my plans.

I've put 10 mu into wheat-maize double cropping, and I'm keeping 2 mu for cotton. I wanted to stop cotton entirely because bending down to pick it kills my back—last year I was still picking in November when the cold wind cut right through my clothes. But Old Wang from the eastern village told me cotton prices were decent last year, and 2 mu is just about manageable if we pick slowly through September and October. More than that and we'd never finish.

For the winter wheat on those 10 mu: I'll sow around October 10th, maybe a day later if it rains. I'm using Jimai 22—I've planted it for years and it doesn't fail me. I bought fresh seed for about 45 yuan per mu because saved seed doesn't sprout as well. For fertilizer, the extension station young man told me I should apply 18 kg of nitrogen per mu based on some soil test, but I've been doing about 15 kg per mu for decades and my wheat is fine. I'll put down 40 kg of compound fertilizer per mu before planting, then topdress with 20 kg of urea per mu in March when the wheat turns green. I can't afford to throw more money at fertilizer—I need to keep cash aside for my husband's blood pressure medicine. I'll irrigate three times: before winter, at jointing, and at grain filling. The electricity bill for pumping hurts, but three times is the minimum. I'll spray herbicide once in spring. I expect about 430 kg per mu if the weather is normal—last year I got 420.

For summer maize on the same 10 mu: This is always the hardest week. We harvest wheat around June 8th, and I need that maize in the ground by June 14th or the frost will get it before it matures. We can't prepare the land ourselves fast enough anymore, so I hire Old Li's tractor for tillage and planting—100 yuan per mu, but it saves us. I'm planting Zhengdan 958, a hybrid. Fifty yuan per mu for seed. I'll apply 40 kg of compound fertilizer at planting, then side-dress with urea when the maize is knee-high. Total nitrogen about 14 kg per mu. I'll irrigate twice if it doesn't rain—once in July when it's growing fast, and once at tasseling. For pesticides, I'll watch for armyworms; last year they were bad in the eastern fields. I hope for 460 kg per mu.

For cotton on the 2 mu: Planting around April 20th. I'm using a local variety that doesn't need as much spraying. I'll put down 30 kg of compound fertilizer per mu as base—that's about 10 kg nitrogen total, which is enough. I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and boll stage. The real cost is labor: my husband and I will pick it ourselves, slowly, over two months. I expect about 220 kg of cotton per mu.

Total input costs will be around 8,000 yuan. It's a lot for us, but we have some savings from last year. I'm keeping 2,000 yuan aside for emergencies though—my husband's medicine, or if the pump breaks. Better safe than sorry.
